newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh poll peaceful despite fraud charge.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh poll peaceful despite fraud charge.

text.p: Bangladesh held generally peaceful parliamentary by-elections on Thursday amid tight security, a big turnout and a few allegations of fraud by opposition candidates, poll officials said.
"The voting was generally peaceful and voters' enthusiasm was remarkable," said one election official in Chittagong.
He said candidates of the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) had alleged that their supporters were intimidated by activists of the ruling Awami League.
"But we have not received any written complaint," he told reporters after voting ended at 4 p.m. (1000 GMT) in the 15 constituencies contested, all outside Dhaka.
Bangladesh held general elections on June 12, with the Awami League winning 146 of the parliament's 300 elected seats. Its leader, Sheikh Hasina, became prime minister on June 23.
The BNP, led by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, won 116 seats, followed by the Jatiya Party of former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad with 32.

Bangladeshi law allows candidates to run in more than one constituency, but they can retain only one. The commission later ordered by-elections in 16 districts vacated by winners who opted to retain other parliamentary seats.
The by-election in the 16th constituency has been delayed.
Thursday's elections were monitored by local and foreign observers. "We can honestly bill it fair and clean," one South Asian diplomat said.

BNP leader Salahuddin Quader Chowdhury, however, told a news conference in Chittagong, his home district, that "opposition candidates had pulled out of many polling centres under pressure from militant Awami activists."
"Ballot boxes were heavily stuffed and intimidation and threats became order of the day. We will demand re-election in these centres," he said.
No such allegations were made in other constituencies.
Nearly 200 people were injured in clashes between supporters of Awami and BNP candidates in the run-up to Thursday's elections, police said.
The election commmission said ballot counting started at 5 p.m. (1100 GMT) and unofficial results for some constituencies should be available late Thursday night.
Awami League leaders said the BNP was looking for a "pretext" to create unrest and disturb the political stability that was restored by the June elections.
